title: Neoteric Finance - Procurement / MSA/DPA / SLAs / Pricing Onboarding

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (Neoteric Head of Procurement), Alan Wu (Neoteric CISO), Rafael Gomez (Neoteric DevOps), Maya Patel (Neoteric Legal), Tom Rivers (Neoteric Finance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Procurement and legal deep-dive. MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs and pricing approvals discussed. Action items captured.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time out. We're here to run through procurement items for the Dedicated+VPC pilot and get clarity on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, and final pricing.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Thanks Lena. We'll be mainly focused on legal and procurement flow today. Maya's on for redlines, Alan's on security. Rafael on the devops side for the pilot.
[00:20] Marcus Chen: Quick intro from my side, I'm Marcus from Redwood infra team, I'll cover the network topology, pilot sizing and SLOs.
[00:28] Alan Wu: Hi, Alan here. Main items for us - encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit logs and data residency. Also need SOC 2 and pen test evidence.
[00:39] Diego Morales: I'll be handling onboarding and support SLAs, happy to map support paths.
[00:45] Rafael Gomez: One ask up front, we need to see expected latency numbers for our longest sequences, and how failover to hosted works if dedicated capacity is saturated.
[00:55] Lena Park: Good, we'll cover latency and fallback behavior. Quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA redlines 2) Security artifacts 3) SLA numbers and penalties 4) Pricing / discounting and signoff process 5) Pilot runbook and timeline.
[01:10] Maya Patel: On MSA - our legal team will likely ask for indemnity language changes and a limitation of liability cap aligned to a year spend. Also DPA needs to include data residency clauses; Neoteric must ensure EU customer data stays in EU region.
[01:28] Lena Park: Understood, we'll share our standard responses. For DPA we support region binding for data at rest and can pin the pilot to eu-west region. Note that in Dedicated+VPC there are extra controls we can enable.
[01:42] Priya Shah: Process wise, procurement needs a final redline set to review. What's your usual turnaround on that?
[01:49] Lena Park: Once you send back redlines we'll route directly to our legal; typical review cycle is 3-5 business days for standard items, but for large liability changes may need extra loop with contracts counsel. We can accelerate if pricing approvals are ready.
[02:05] Tom Rivers: On pricing - we have internal thresholds. What's the discount stack for a 12-month committed Dedicated plan?
[02:12] Lena Park: We can offer tiered discounts for committed capacity. For a 12-month reserved commit we typically provide X% off list and volume pricing on tokens and dedicated throughput. I'll share a pricing worksheet after the call.
[02:25] Marcus Chen: On technical SLAs - for Dedicated we target 99.9% uptime and tail latency SLOs (p95/p99) that we can calibrate to your latency targets; if you need stricter SLOs we can discuss higher service levels with financial credits.
[02:40] Alan Wu: We need written SLAs with credits and an RTO/RPO statement for data. Also need audit logs for each inference request tied to request IDs and KMS key usage logs.
[02:52] Marcus Chen: We emit request-level tracing and can surface per-route logs; KMS integration for envelope encryption is standard. There was a small note - sometimes our transcripting of environment names gets mangled, but the capability is there.
[03:06] Rafael Gomez: About fallback - if Dedicated is saturated will traffic automatically route to hosted? We don't want customer data leaving region or environment.
[03:14] Lena Park: Good question. Fallback is policy driven; we can set strict region + tenancy constraints so traffic won't leave your VPC. Alternatively, we can enable fallback to a verified model variant inside the same region under a lower capacity fallback policy.
[03:29] Priya Shah: For data residency we need the DPA to explicitly state no egress of EU personal data outside EU without prior consent.
[03:36] Lena Park: We'll add that clause in proposed redlines.
[03:40] Maya Patel: About liability - our procurement is pushing for liability cap at 2x annual payment. Is that something you can accept?
[03:47] Lena Park: Our standard is generally capped at fees paid in prior 12 months; we can discuss moving to 2x for enterprise contracts but that usually ties to board-level signoff and procurement. We can flag it to contracts now.
[03:59] Alan Wu: On encryption, we need to bring our HSM vendor into the conversation if you require key import. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM?
[04:10] Marcus Chen: Yes - we support both cloud KMS and bring-your-own key material for on-prem HSM integrations. There are a few steps for key rotation and agent install in the VPC. We'll document those in the runbook.
[04:28] Rafael Gomez: Okay, runbook will be useful. Also curious about patching windows for model updates - what's your recommended cadence and outage expectations?
[04:36] Marcus Chen: Model updates are handled via canary rollouts; dedicated pools can be configured for staggered updates to avoid full pool downtime. Typical maintenance windows are configurable, and we aim for zero-downtime for inferencing by draining connections. We'll include the rollout plan in the pilot doc.
[04:55] Tom Rivers: Back to pricing - if you can share the precise sheet today we'll need to route to procurement and finance. Any incentives for faster signoff?
[05:03] Lena Park: For committed signups we can offer an onboarding discount and prioritized SLA terms. We'll mark that in the worksheet.
[05:11] Priya Shah: On the DPA, we need subprocessor list and a requirement for prior notice before onboarding new subprocessors.
[05:18] Diego Morales: We'll attach current subprocessor list and include a notice period clause. It's standard for enterprise customers.
[05:28] Maya Patel: Also need clarity on logs retention and deletion process after contract termination.
[05:33] Lena Park: DPA will specify retention windows and secure deletion procedures; we can align retention to your policy (e.g., 90 days logs, with option for 30/365 depending on account level).
[05:45] Alan Wu: For incident response, we need SOC/TLP levels on notifications and a runbook for security incidents.
[05:51] Diego Morales: We have an incident playbook and SLA for incident acknowledgement and remediation timelines. We'll include contact points.
[06:03] Rafael Gomez: One more question on observability - will we get token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route? That's critical for our chargebacks.
[06:13] Marcus Chen: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route latency and tracing, and can export to your billing system. We'll show an example in the pilot dashboard.
[06:25] Priya Shah: Good. From procurement side our timeline is: legal redlines by EOD next Tuesday (2026-10-27), procurement approval by end of week after that, finance sign-off same week. Can you meet that?
[06:38] Lena Park: Yes, that's tight but doable. We'll prioritize sending artifacts this week so you have time to review.
[06:45] Tom Rivers: Who from Redwood will handle price approvals?
[06:49] Lena Park: I'll own the pricing sheet and work with our finance ops. Diego will support contractual SLAs. Marcus will own technical items.
[06:59] Maya Patel: Will you accept our standard redline format (tracked changes PDF)?
[07:03] Lena Park: Yes, send tracked changes to contracts@redwood.ai and loop me in, I'll route internally.
[07:12] Priya Shah: Anything about insurance requirements? We usually require 1M cyber liability.
[07:18] Diego Morales: Our standard insurance levels are aligned with enterprise requirements; we'll confirm certs and include in the contract packet.
[07:26] Alan Wu: Pen testing - do you supply recent pentest results or accept our vendor to run an external pentest with a scoped plan?
[07:34] Marcus Chen: We can share recent pentest summaries; for customer-specific pen tests we usually do a scoped engagement. We'll coordinate with your security team.
[07:45] Rafael Gomez: Are there any limitations on model weights? Eg. you mentioned model variants, will we be able to pin or upload private models?
[07:53] Marcus Chen: For Private deployments and certain Dedicated plans we support pinned model versions and customer-supplied models on approved hardware; we'll need to review licensing for model weights.
[08:05] Lena Park: Ok recapping - action items: we'll send MSA/DPA with suggested redlines, SOC 2 and security artifacts, pricing worksheet with committed discounting, and pilot runbook + architecture. Customer will return legal redlines and procurement timeline.
[08:20] Priya Shah: Sounds good. One final ask - can you provide a sample SLR showing credit calculations for SLA breaches? We need that in our legal packet.
[08:28] Diego Morales: Yes, we'll include SLR examples and a sample SLA credit schedule.
[08:35] Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll review and aim to get redlines to you by 2026-10-23.
[08:42] Lena Park: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet today.
[08:47] Tom Rivers: Thanks, bye.
[08:49] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K-V cash for KV cache), speaker labels sometimes generic.
notes: References: pricing worksheet (link sent post-call), MSA draft (will be attached), DPA template, SOC 2 report. Customer prefers tracked-changes PDF for legal redlines. Pilot target start in ~2 weeks pending approvals.
